title: Wage board: owners offer Tk 15,800, workers cut demand to Tk 22,000
excerpt: A near nine-hour wage board meeting ended without a deal on Monday. Talks resume this afternoon as protests kept about 55 Gazipur factories idle.

image.alt: Women workers at sewing machines on a garment factory floor in Bangladesh
image.credit: Tareq Salahuddin from Dhaka, Bangladesh / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 2.0

content:
Garment factory owners have offered a minimum wage of Tk 15,800 a month, and workers have lowered their demand to Tk 22,000, Prothom Alo reported. Both sides revised their figures twice during the third meeting of the Minimum Wage Board on Monday (23 November). The meeting ran from about 11:45am to 8:30pm and was adjourned without a decision. It resumes at 2pm today.

Owners opened Monday's session at Tk 15,000. Workers had submitted a demand of Tk 32,000 at the board's second meeting. The current minimum for entry-level garment workers is Tk 12,500.

The meeting at the board's Segunbagicha office was chaired by Syed Azad Subhani. BGMEA president Mahmud Hasan Khan joined as an expert for the owners, and Rashedul Alam, general secretary of the Bangladesh Mukto Garments Sramik Union Federation, joined for the workers. The chairman told reporters that findings from the board's visits to small, medium and large factories had been presented and were being debated.

Workers protested in Gazipur and Savar again on Monday. Production stopped at about 55 factories in the Gazipur area, Prothom Alo reported.

Why it matters

The gap between the two offers is still Tk 6,200 a month. For garment workers, most of them women, the figure will set pay for the next several years. Unrest has already shut hundreds of factories this month, and union leaders have been arrested. Rights groups, legal aid NGOs and organisations working with women workers will be watching both the number and how the protests are policed.

What to watch

Whether today's session reaches a figure, whether the board publishes a draft for public comment, and whether factories in Gazipur, Savar and Ashulia reopen. The new wage is due to take effect in December.
